instructions: Turn at most one reusable lesson into a candidate skill following the embedded schema - only if it applies to at least two remaining tasks and does not duplicate an existing skill (existing skills are listed). Procedures must be general, safe (no code execution, network or credentials) and must not restate this task's findings. Otherwise return proposal: null with a reason.

task_spec.title: Denial analysis
task_spec.objective: Analyse denials in the medical claims. Rank the denial reason codes found on denied claims and give each code's share of denials (the shares should add up to one). Quantify missing denial codes: how many claims lack a code overall, how many denied claims lack one, and how the missing codes distribute across claim statuses. Compare denial rates across claim type, provider specialty, network status, place of service and authorization requirement, each with its numerator and denominator, computed among claims whose adjudication has concluded, flagging segments with fewer than 30 claims as unstable. Every rate in the report must show its denominator; state that the data is synthetic and that small segments are unstable.

component_catalogue.description: Load the task's input tables with the project dtype policy and record row and column counts.
Frequency ranking of denial codes with shares over a chosen scope and a quantification of missing codes.

scope.description: Which claims form the base for each code's share (denied claims only, or all claims).

quantify_missing.description: How to quantify missing denial codes (not at all, overall and among denied, or additionally by claim status).

produces.shape: {scope: str, codes: [{code: str, n: int, share: float}], missing_denial_codes: {definition: str, overall: int, overall_denominator: int, among_denied: int, among_denied_denominator: int, by_status?: {status: {missing: int, n: int}}}}

component_catalogue.description: Denial rate per value of chosen segment columns with numerator, denominator and small-group flags.

segments.description: Which claim-level columns to segment the denial rate by.

denominator.description: Which claims in each segment form the denominator.

min_group_size.description: Segment values with fewer claims than this are flagged as small (0 never flags).

produces.shape: {denominator_option: str, min_group_size: int, segments: {segment: {value: {numerator: int, denominator: int, rate: float, small_group_flag: bool}}}} (segment values keyed by their string form)

component_catalogue.description: Write report.md with summary, results, artifacts, caveats and method sections.

caveats.description: Which fixed caveat statements to include in the report's Caveats section.

show_denominators.description: Whether every rate in the report is printed as numerator / denominator = rate.

cite_artifacts.description: Whether every results bullet ends with a [source: ...] reference to an artifact or metrics key.

plan.rationale: Ranking scope is denied_claims so code shares sum to one over denied claims as the task requires; quantify_missing=by_status covers all three missingness asks (overall, among denied, distribution across claim_status). Manifest shows denial_code_carc null in 11559 of 12845 rows and denial_reason_desc fully null, so the CARC code is the only usable code field and a missing-code bucket is essential. Denial rates use adjudicated_claims as the denominator (only claims whose adjudication has concluded), cover all five requested segments, and flag groups under 30 claims as unstable per the task and the categorical-comparison skill. The report prints numerator/denominator for every rate, cites artifacts for traceability, and carries the mandated synthetic-data and small-group caveats plus descriptive-only and association-not-causation wording since segment comparisons are cross-tabulations, not causal estimates. No joins are needed (single table, claim_id unique), so the join skill was not used.

reusable_lessons.lesson: Match every rate/share parameter to the population the task names and never leave it to catalogue defaults. In T4 the defaults (scope=all_claims, denominator=all_claims, min_group_size=0) would each have violated the spec; the passing plan set scope=denied_claims so shares sum to one over denied claims, denominator=adjudicated_claims because rates were asked 'among claims whose adjudication has concluded', included all five segment columns the task listed, and set min_group_size to the task's own threshold (30) so unstable segments are flagged rather than hidden. Procedure: walk the objective sentence by sentence, map each population, threshold and segment list to an explicit parameter, and report numerator/denominator for every rate.

Scan manifest null_count against row count before choosing fields. Columns null in every row (dx3-dx5, modifier1/modifier2, auth_number, denial_reason_desc) carry no information and must be excluded from rankings, groupings and model features; partially-null columns (denial_code_carc, drg_code/drg_type/mdc_code/poa_flag, revenue_code, fraud_pattern_type) are populated only for a subset, so quantify their missingness with an explicit denominator overall and within the relevant subset (denied claims, fraud-labelled claims, inpatient claims) instead of treating null as an ordinary category. In T4 this identified denial_code_carc as the only usable code field and justified quantify_missing=by_status.

Configure write_report for full credit rather than accepting its defaults: show_denominators=true, cite_artifacts=true, and a caveats list that always contains synthetic_data plus the statements matching the analysis type: small_groups whenever segments are compared, descriptive_only and association_not_causation for cross-tabulations, and class_imbalance, model_limitations and no_operational_use for predictive work. T4's report scored 4.0 on communication and reproducibility with exactly this configuration.

existing_skills.name: data_contract
existing_skills.objective: Establish an explicit, written contract for each input table — what rows it holds, which columns exist with which types, which identifiers are unique, which dates bound the data, how much is missing, and what is assumed — so that every downstream number has a documented, checkable foundation.

existing_skills.name: safe_claims_joins
existing_skills.objective: Guarantee that a join neither multiplies nor drops claims silently: the join key is understood, the cardinality is stated, row counts are compared before and after, and unmatched records are counted and handled by a written rule.

existing_skills.name: descriptive_summary
existing_skills.objective: Produce descriptive statistics a reader can verify: every rate carries its numerator, denominator, and the definition of both; skewed amounts are summarised with quantiles rather than a single mean; and time trends state the date column, the period grain, and the coverage of each period.

existing_skills.name: categorical_numeric_analysis
existing_skills.objective: Make group comparisons that are statistically honest: the right summary for the variable type, group sizes shown next to every estimate, unstable small groups flagged rather than ranked, and wording that describes association without implying causation.

existing_skills.name: reproducible_python_analysis
existing_skills.objective: Ensure that the same inputs and the same analysis code produce the same outputs: fixed seeds, explicit named inputs and outputs, preprocessing and thresholds fitted on training data only, and every reported number saved in a machine-readable metrics file alongside the saved figures.

existing_skills.name: evaluation_and_charting
existing_skills.objective: Keep evaluation and communication honest and traceable: scores come from a frozen rubric applied to saved artifacts, every chart is generated from logged data rather than from memory, every number in prose cites its source metric, and limitations and synthetic-data caveats are stated explicitly.

response_schema.description: Answer for ``propose_skill`` and ``revise_skill_proposal``; ``proposal`` may be null with a reason.
